reason: The cited evidence (E1) explicitly shows that coherent nanoprecipitates in an fcc FeCoNi-based HEA increase strength with only a marginal coercivity increase (<10.7 Oe), supporting the premise that coherent precipitates cause minimal wall pinning. However, E1 provides no data on incoherent precipitates, so the key premises that incoherent precipitates will strongly pin walls and raise coercivity well above 100 Oe without harming saturation magnetization are unsupported by the cited passage.
premises: Incoherent precipitates create local strain fields and misfit dislocations that strongly pin domain walls
Coherent nanoprecipitates introduce minimal domain wall pinning
The proposed incoherent precipitates will raise coercivity well above 100 Oe without significantly reducing saturation magnetization
The fcc FeCoNi matrix can be retained while forming incoherent nanoprecipitates through composition and heat-treatment adjustments
